thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Drop As Tech Pullback, Nissan CEO's Arrest Takes Toll

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Drop As Tech Pullback, Nissan CEO's Arrest Takes Toll
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Auto, electronics sectors weigh Nikkei; tech stocks sink Hang Seng
Asian stock markets fell in early trading Tuesday, following tech-led declines on Wall Street.
Japan's Nikkei was down 0.8%, with electronics and machinery stocks among the biggest decliners. Sony (6758.TO) was down 2.6% while Fanuc (6954.TO) and Hitachi (6501.TO) were off some 3%. But the auto sector was the most watched, following the arrest of Nissan CEO Carlos Ghosn on Monday. Alliance partners Nissan (NSANY) and Mitsubishi (7211.TO) slid in early trading, with Nissan at almost-2 1/2 -year lows. But rival Toyota (7203.TO) benefited, climbing 2%.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 1.3%, with Tencent (0700.HK) down 2.5% and smartphone-component firms AAC (2018.HK) and Sunny Optical (2382.HK) off some 2%. Xiaomi (1810.HK) jumped 5% after its third-quarter earnings report
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite was down 1.2% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite dropped 1.4%. Among large caps, real estate was off 1.3% after yesterday's sharp bounce. Financials, which also were strong Monday, pulled back 0.9%.
A report about another round of production cuts for iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-apple-iphone-suppliers-extend-losses-after-wsj-report-of-further-production-cuts-2018-11-19)weighed on Apple (AAPL) suppliers in Asia. Taiwan's Taiex fell 0.5% as product assembler Hon Hai (2317.TW) dropped 2.7% to hit fresh five-year lows and Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) declined 1.3%. Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix (000660.SE) slid another 2.7% and Samsung Electronics (005930.SE) lost 1.7% as the Kospi dropped 0.6%.
Australia's benchmark index was down 0.8%, and New Zealand and Singapore posted losses as well.
